summary: Mobile Wi‑Fi suspend causes SSE half‑close: final paragraph missing on resume, client sees duplicate prefix tokens
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ChatWrite Inc., dedicated) reports reproducible loss of final paragraph and duplicated prefix tokens when their mobile web client goes to background (Wi‑Fi sleep) and then resumes. The SSE connection experiences a half‑close while the client OS suspends sockets; upon reconnect the resumed stream is missing the final epilogue and the beginning tokens are replayed/duplicated.

Impact:
- Several production users see truncated outputs (missing final sentence or closing paragraph) in ~0.8% of streaming responses from the redwood/gptx-16k-v1 model in us-east-1.
- Customer's chat UX shows repeated initial fragment plus truncated ending, causing poor UX and increased retries.
- Affects mobile web users on iOS/Android when devices suspend background network sockets.

Environment:
- Cluster: prod-us-east (api-gateway + managed serving-runtime pool, dedicated capacity for ChatWrite namespace)
- Model: redwood/gptx-16k-v1 pinned by customer
- Client: ChatWrite web app using Redwood JS SDK v0.9.3 (SSE mode).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a streaming chat completion on mobile web (iOS Safari / Android Chrome) using SSE endpoint with a ~1k token response.
2) Put the phone into background for ~15–30s (device enters low‑power Wi‑Fi state).
3) Bring the app back to foreground; client reconnects to SSE and attempts resume via existing conversation id/last_event_id.
4) Observe: beginning of the response is duplicated (replayed prefix) and the final paragraph / concluding sentence is missing.

Observed behavior:
- On resume the client receives the same prefix tokens it had before suspension, then the stream ends without an explicit end event.
- Server logs show an upstream half‑close/h1 204 from the LB at approximately the suspend time and no explicit 'end_choice' event emitted for affected responses.
- Resume attempt includes last_event_id but resume sequence numbers don't align with server's half‑closed state, leading to a silent termination rather than a reissue of the missing tail.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should either stitch missing suffix correctly or return a clear terminal event (end_of_stream/choice_end) so client can surface a deterministic error and/or request a retry.

Logs / artifacts attached (references):
- Customer trace id: cw-trace-20260313-8421 (provided)
- Sample server logs (trimmed): logs/prod/us-east/serving-runtime/2026-03-13/trace-cw-8421.log (S3 link in ticket).
- LB probe & connection events: lb-us-east-probes-2026-03-13.log (S3 link).
- Client network capture (customer): ChatWrite_capture_2026-03-13.pcap (attached).

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Increase client reconnection backoff and enable client-side deduplication based on incremental token sequence if using SDK v0.9.3 (we provided a small snippet).
- If possible, switch to websocket streaming (WS) which does a full rehandshake and avoids the LB half‑close race in most cases.

Investigation notes (SRE/Support):
- Reproduced internally using an emulator that simulates TCP socket close on background suspend. Observed the same pattern: LB (haproxy fronting) sends a half‑close health probe/idle reset, upstream serving runtime finishes streaming but never emits the final end event due to a race with socket closure handling.
- Hypothesis: When the client socket is suspended the LB/edge treats the connection as idle and tethers a probe that triggers a graceful half‑close on the fronting connection. The serving runtime, upon detecting the half‑close, winds down the in‑flight response path without emitting the final JSON terminal frame (end_choice). The resume path attempts to replay from a last_event_id anchored to the prior session; however the server's per‑session resume state has been purged or advanced so server responds with a short reissue that doesn't include the missing epilogue.
- Evidence: correlating timestamps between lb log (probe reset at 15:02:12), serving-runtime partial stream completion (15:02:12.123), and client reconnect (15:02:42) shows the missing end event window.
- Similar patterns seen in INT-4382 (internal LB idle timeout tests) and a small subset of customer reports.

Temporary mitigation implemented (SRE):
- Adjusted haproxy idle_probe window on a subset of fronting nodes for ChatWrite dedicated capacity to 45s (previously 15s) as a canary.
- Patch queued for serving-runtime (PR referenced) to ensure explicit end_of_choice emission even on upstream half‑close; will also persist a short resume buffer to allow correct stitching when clients reconnect within 60s.

Action plan / next steps:
1) Roll out haproxy probe window change to all nodes for ChatWrite namespace (SRE), target 2026-03-15 04:00 UTC. (owner: Daniel Kim)
2) Merge PR in serving-runtime that forces terminal event emission on half‑close and adds a 60s ephemeral resume buffer for recently closed sessions. Test plan: unit tests + canary in staging + canary in prod. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2187 (owner: eng/sam-chen). Target: 2026-03-18.
3) SDK: publish guidance and a small dedupe helper in SDK v0.9.4 that identifies duplicate prefixes based on incremental token sequence ids. (owner: DevX / Priya Rao). Target: 2026-03-16.
4) Post‑mortem decision: evaluate increasing default probe windows for mobile‑heavy customer lanes and implement streaming end markers in protocol docs. (owner: SRE/Product).

Resolution notes (planned):
- Short term: LB probe window increased for ChatWrite (partial canary active). Customer verified reduction in reproduce rate in test sessions.
- Medium term: runtime patch to emit terminal events + resume buffer (pending PR merge and canary).

Customer communication plan:
- Notified customer on 2026-03-13 of an SRE canary and workaround. Will follow up with an engineering postmortem after full rollout and testing.
